newsitem.title: USA: Talks continue between GM, UAW.
newsitem.headline: Talks continue between GM, UAW.

text.p: Talks continued Wednesday aimed at reaching two new contracts between the United Auto Workers union and General Motors Corp., while union members at a third plant were expected to approve a tentative contract.
UAW Local 455 President Dennis Fiting said the roughly 1,000 members who work at a GM foundry in Saginaw, Mich., will finish voting about 11:30 p.m. Wednesday.
"We're optimistic it's going to pass," he said.
Bargainers for the union and GM reached a tentative settlement late Friday, averting a strike at the plant, makes pistons, piston rods and transmission parts for a variety of GM vehicles.

Fiting said the company agreed to add 20 skilled trade jobs and 60 production positions. GM also agreed to contract language that limits outsourcing for the life of the agreement and provides job security for workers in skilled trades.
GM also agreed to pay signing bonuses to skilled trades workers worth $225,000. That amounts to about $760 per person, he said.

Meantime, union and company officials said talks continued at a Grand Rapids, Mich., metal fabricating plant. Union officials at Local 730 have extended the strike deadline since the original 11:59 p.m. Friday, June 13, deadline.
Bargainers resumed work at 8 a.m. Wednesday after talking until about 9 p.m. Tuesday, said GM spokesman Peter Ternes.
The plant, which has 2,346 workers, produces sheet metal parts for several GM vehicles. Workers have previously voted down an earlier tentative agreement.

Negotiations are also going on to resolve a strike at GM's Pontiac, Mich., full-size pickup truck plant. Gene Caverly, a spokesman for UAW Local 594, said bargainers have been talking into the evening.
About 5,800 workers at the factory have been off the job since April 22, when talks broke down over staffing levels and other issues.
A strike was averted Tuesday when GM and UAW Local 1866 reached a tentative contract at a key Wisconsin plant that makes catalytic converters.
GM stock fell 25 cents to $56.75 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
